reference: If she books another hour, the therapy will continue next week.
sk: Ak si zapíše ďalšiu hodinu, terapia bude pokračovať aj budúci týždeň.
cz: Jestli si zapíše další hodinu, terapie bude pokračovat i příští týden.
acceptable: If {she|he} {books|schedules|signs up for} {another|one more|an extra} {hour|session}, the therapy will {also |}continue next week.
If {she|he} {books|schedules|signs up for} {another|one more|an extra} {hour|session}, the therapy will continue next week {too|as well}.
If {she|he} {books|schedules} {another|one more} {hour|session}, therapy will {also |}continue next week.
The therapy will {also |}continue next week if {she|he} {books|schedules} {another|one more} {hour|session}.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} will book another hour, the therapy will continue next week.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „if“ patrí v First Conditional Present Simple: „if she books“, nie „will book“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „if“ patří ve First Conditional Present Simple: „if she books“, ne „will book“.
mistakes.feedback_en: In First Conditional use Present Simple after “if”: “if she books”, not “will book”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} books another hour, the therapy continues next week.
mistakes.feedback_sk: V First Conditional patrí do hlavnej vety „will“, lebo ide o budúci následok: „will continue“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Ve First Conditional patří do hlavní věty „will“, protože jde o budoucí následek: „will continue“.
mistakes.feedback_en: First Conditional uses “will” for the future result: “will continue”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} books another hour, the therapy will continues next week.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „will“ patrí vždy základný tvar slovesa bez -s: „will continue“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „will“ patří vždy základní tvar slovesa bez -s: „will continue“.
mistakes.feedback_en: After “will” always use the base verb without -s: “will continue”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} books another hour, the therapy will continue the next week.
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Budúci týždeň“ je „next week“ bez „the“; „the next week“ znamená nasledujúcich sedem dní.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Příští týden“ je „next week“ bez „the“; „the next week“ znamená následujících sedm dní.
mistakes.feedback_en: Say “next week” without “the”; “the next week” means the following seven days.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} books other hour, the therapy will continue next week.
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Ďalšiu hodinu“ je „another hour“; „other“ sa pred jednotným číslom samo nepoužíva.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Další hodinu“ je „another hour“; „other“ se před jednotným číslem samo nepoužívá.
mistakes.feedback_en: “One more hour” is “another hour”; “other” is not used alone before a singular noun.

source_issues: Slovak “aj” / Czech “i” (also) has no equivalent in the English reference; versions with “also/too/as well” are accepted.
Slovak and Czech drop the subject pronoun, so “she” is not given; “he” is accepted too.
